1.speaker: meera
1.text: Tara! Mohan! Please, call my children. Tell them their mother has come back.
1.sfx_cue: police station gate clangs, crowd murmuring

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Stop there. Do not cross the desk until I ask you.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Then ask quickly. I have waited... I have waited long enough.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Your name.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Meera. Devraj's daughter. Tara and Mohan's mother.

1.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
1.text: She says she is the dead woman.

1.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
1.text: Call her father. Let him see her face.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: He will know me. Bring him here. Please.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Constable, shut the gate. Nobody leaves, and nobody touches her.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Move aside. I will settle this.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Baba...

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Do not call me that.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Look at me. Properly. The cut above my eyebrow, I got it on your grain scale. You carried me home.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Many people have scars.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Your left knee hurts before you sit. You hide money inside the red account book. Baba, please... just hold my hand.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Do not touch me.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: One touch. You will know.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: I buried my daughter. I placed wood on her pyre with these hands. You are an impostor.

1.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
1.text: Her own father will not touch her.

1.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
1.text: Someone trained her. Why else would she come here?

1.speaker: meera
1.text: I came for my children. Where are Tara and Mohan?

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: My grandchildren have already suffered. They will not be displayed before a stranger.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: They are not your shield. Bring them.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Sub-inspector, remove this woman before Tara hears this filth in the market.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: No. She entered a police station and made an identity claim. We record it before anyone removes anyone.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: The police recorded her death. Is your own record now a rumour?

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: One fact at a time. Meera, when did you last see your children?

1.speaker: meera
1.text: The morning I disappeared. Tara would not drink her milk. Mohan had fever... no, the fever began the night before.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: All of that was discussed after the funeral. Anyone in Dharmapur could repeat it.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Not this. Mohan called fever medicine bitter rain. Tara drew a moustache on the bottle so he would laugh.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: Enough.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: You know that happened.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: I know grief makes foolish people generous with information.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Babulal, bring the death entry and the original identification file.

1.speaker: babulal
1.text: Madam, that file is sealed with the murder case.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Then open the cupboard, not the seal.

1.speaker: babulal
1.text: If the woman is genuine, every connected page will have to be reviewed.

1.speaker: devraj
1.text: If. Please remember that word.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: Show me what you wrote about me.

1.speaker: babulal
1.text: There is a death certificate, cremation acknowledgement, family identification and a station register entry.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: And my children were made to live under those pages.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: Give me the date and status.

1.speaker: babulal
1.text: Fourteenth November, two thousand twenty-two. Meera, daughter of Devraj, recorded deceased.

1.speaker: meera
1.text: I am standing in front of you.

1.speaker: babulal
1.text: The station register still lists Meera as dead.

1.speaker: kavita
1.text: And four men are in jail for murdering her.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: If that woman goes near Tara or Mohan, I will hold this station responsible for what it does to them.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Your concern is noted. Now step away from the door.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Do not send him away. Let him hear every answer.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: No. Private details are useful only when the crowd cannot feed them to you.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: She already knows enough to perform.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: You will wait outside until I call you.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: This is my daughter's case.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: That is precisely why you do not conduct the test.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: Very well. Test her. But do not mistake confidence for truth.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Close it.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: How long before I see my children?

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: When I can put you near them without turning two children into evidence.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: They are already evidence. Everyone outside is saying their mother's name.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Sit. One fact at a time.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: I cannot sit quietly while Baba calls me an impostor.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Then sit angrily.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: You think I am lying.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: I think the register says you are dead, you say you are alive, and four prisoners cannot both have murdered you and not murdered you.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Ask me something.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: What did Devraj break on the day Tara was born?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Nothing. He claimed the tea glass broke by itself. Actually, he squeezed it when the nurse said the baby was a girl.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Where did the glass cut him?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Between his thumb and first finger. He hid the bandage before entering my room.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: What did he bring you?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Two oranges and the wrong slippers. Both were for the right foot.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: What colour?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Green, with silver flowers. I wore them anyway because he looked so ashamed.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Mohan's first word.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Not Ma. Everyone says Ma. It was wheel. He pointed at Baba's bicycle and said it until he slept.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: What frightens Tara?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: People knowing she is frightened. She will stand near any snake if someone is watching. Alone, she cannot even touch a shed snakeskin.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: That answer may matter later.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: It matters now. Bring her.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Not yet.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: You keep saying not yet. I heard that for months. Food, not yet. Outside, not yet. Home... not yet.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Who said that to you?

2.speaker: meera
2.text: I will give a full statement. First let my children see my face.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Your conditions do not control this inquiry.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: And my father's fear should not control it either.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Correct.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Then why is he still the one deciding who I am?

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: He is not.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Devraj. Come in alone.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: Has she failed?

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: She answered six questions. Four match your earlier family statement exactly. Two were never in the file.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: Then someone in the family spoke carelessly.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Say my name once while looking at me.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: I will not reward manipulation.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Did you break a tea glass when Tara was born?

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: I may have. That was many years ago.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Did you bring two right-foot slippers?

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: Small family stories travel. Evidence does not.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: You said you brought evidence.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: I did.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: The hospital photographed the burned body before identification. I identified the tattoo and the black thread tied at the wrist.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: My mother tied that thread after Mohan's fever. I never removed it.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: The body had the same thread. The same tattoo. That is why I signed.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Describe your tattoo without looking at the photograph.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Three dots above a small crooked leaf. The woman made the last line too deep. It is here, on my left hand.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: A tattoo can be copied after the case becomes public.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: After? Look closely. The leaf has stretched with my skin. This is not new.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Babulal, bring the identification record.

2.speaker: babulal
2.text: Madam, the hospital note says black thread at wrist and tattoo visible beside it.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: Does it specify left or right?

2.speaker: babulal
2.text: No. Only the photograph shows the side.

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: I saw the mark. I had just lost my daughter. Do not examine my grief as though it were a crime.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: I am examining the identification.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Which hand?

2.speaker: devraj
2.text: The image may have been reversed during printing.

2.speaker: babulal
2.text: The hospital number is readable, not reversed.

2.speaker: meera
2.text: Which hand, madam? Please... say it.

2.speaker: kavita
2.text: The photograph shows the tattoo on the body is on the opposite hand from Meera's tattoo.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Open the gate. My children are inside that house.
3.sfx_cue: police jeep brakes, iron house gate rattles

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: You enter under police guard, and you do not force either child to approach you.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: I am not forcing them. I am coming home.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: This has not been her home since the cremation.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: You burned another woman's body and gave away my room. Neither act changes whose house this is.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: The body identification is under review. Do not state conclusions before the evidence does.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Then let the evidence open the gate.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I will open it.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Tara.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Do not call me like that.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Like what?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Like you have been searching every room and finally found me.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: That is exactly how I am calling you.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Sub-inspector, you said she was only coming to look at the house.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: She is here to identify private details. You may stay, or you may leave the room.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I am staying.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Where is Mohan?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: He does not want to see you.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: That is not what I said!

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Mohan? Open the door, little wheel.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: No!

3.speaker: tara
3.text: He locked himself in the storeroom when the jeep came.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: He is frightened.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: He is confused. There is a difference.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: This is why I refused. The boy has already mourned once.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Because you told him I was ashes.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: Because I identified his mother's body.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Enough. Tara, show us the rooms without giving her clues.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Fine. If she is my mother, she should not need clues.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: I do not.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Then start here. What was kept in that wall niche?

3.speaker: meera
3.text: The brass lamp. Except during exams, when you hid your school timetable behind it.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Anybody could have seen the lamp.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Nobody saw the sums you wrote on the wall behind the timetable. Seven times eight was fifty-four until I made you correct it.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I was small.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: You cried because the wrong answer looked neater.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: Tara, you do not have to listen.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I said I am staying.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Next room.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: What was under the bed?

3.speaker: meera
3.text: A steel trunk, one broken sandal and Mohan whenever he stole jaggery.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: I did not steal it.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: No. The jaggery climbed into your pocket by itself.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: Maybe.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Open the door. I will not come close. I only want to see how tall you are.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: If I open it, will the police take you away?

3.speaker: meera
3.text: I don't... I cannot promise what the police will do. But I will not leave without telling you.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: No one is taking her away today unless evidence requires it.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: That is not a promise.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: No. It is the truth.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Mohan, remember the tune I used when your chest hurt?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Do not sing it.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Why?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Because he wants you to be her. He will believe anything if you use her voice.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: My voice did not die because you were told I did.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: You know stories. You know rooms. You even look like the photographs. But I will not call you mother.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Not today?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Not until I decide.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: You have heard her. This visit should end.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: No. My room is left.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: That room is used for storage now.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Then your storage is sleeping in my room.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Open it.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: There is nothing relevant inside.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: You do not decide relevance.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: The blue wall is gone.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: It was painted after the funeral.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: My mirror was on that nail. The cot faced east. I kept Tara's first school ribbon inside the mirror frame.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: The mirror broke years ago.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Then the ribbon may still be behind the loose brick below the nail.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Tara, were you aware of that hiding place?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: No.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: There are dozens of loose bricks in an old house.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Third brick from the corner. It has a white scratch shaped like a hook.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Do not help her. I will check.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: There is something inside.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: A faded school ribbon, blue and white.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: You cried on your first morning, Tara. So I cut my own blue scarf and tied a matching ribbon around my wrist.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: A hidden object proves you knew this house. It does not prove why you left it.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: I did not leave you willingly.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: There. Now comes the accusation that protects her from every question.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: She has not given the allegation yet.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: I will. But not while he turns every word into shame.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Then answer me without him. Why did you not come back?

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Because I could not. Because every time I thought I had a road home, someone closed it. I tried to remember your faces exactly, but Mohan kept growing in my head and you... you stayed thirteen.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I was fourteen when you disappeared.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: No. Your birthday was eleven days later. I had hidden your present in the grain drum.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: What present?

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Red glass bangles. You said you were too old for dolls and too young for gold. I never got to give them to you.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: Tara, enough. Pain is not proof.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: I know.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: Is she crying?

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Stay inside, Mohan.

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: I want to see her.

3.speaker: tara
3.text: Then why did you lock the door?

3.speaker: mohan
3.text: Because if she is not Ma, I will lose her again.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: You do not have to open it today. I will sit outside.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: You will not occupy this courtyard until the village accepts you.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: The village does not issue identity certificates.

3.speaker: devraj
3.text: The village will still remember who brought scandal to its doors.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: And it will remember who refused evidence when it was placed in his hand.

3.speaker: VOICE AT GATE
3.text: Police! I have come from the Kota bus stand. I need the officer handling the returned woman's case.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Who are you?

3.speaker: BUS STAND VENDOR
3.text: I run the tea counter beside the departure bays. Her face was in today's paper.

3.speaker: meera
3.text: Where did you get that?

3.speaker: BUS STAND VENDOR
3.text: It was behind an old timetable at my counter. I remember the day because these two waited there for three hours.

3.speaker: kavita
3.text: Which two?

3.speaker: BUS STAND VENDOR
3.text: This photograph shows Meera standing beside Raghav.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: That photograph proves only one thing. Meera left Dharmapur with me because she wanted to abandon her marriage and her children.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Let me ask him one question.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: You will speak when the committee permits it.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: This is a police verification, not a punishment meeting. She may question the man in the photograph.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Certainly. A truthful man does not fear questions.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Where was this photograph taken?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Kota bus stand.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Which platform?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: There are no platforms at that counter. Only benches.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: So you recognise the place.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: I have worked in transport for twelve years. I recognise hundreds of counters.

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: Ask why my daughter was standing beside him.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Your daughter? Yesterday, I was a stranger bringing scandal to your courtyard.

4.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
4.text: He called her an impostor inside the police station.

4.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
4.text: Now he needs her to be his daughter, because the photograph is public.

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: The committee did not summon the street to judge me.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: No. The evidence did.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: Raghav, explain the photograph from the beginning.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Meera approached me privately. She said she was unhappy at home. She asked for transport to Kota.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: That is a lie.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: You asked me to speak. Please allow me the courtesy of finishing.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Courtesy? You watched while I was taken away.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Meera, taken by whom?

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: I don't... I did not know his name then. Raghav spoke to him near the tea counter.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: She means Shahid. He was arranging labour transport that week.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: You know which man she means without hearing a description.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Because she has made this accusation before. Confused stories travel quickly in a village.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: I have not spoken Shahid's name in this village.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Then perhaps your story reached Dharmapur before you did.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: Answer plainly. Did Meera travel with you willingly?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Yes. She sat beside me for three hours. She drank tea. She could have called for help.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: You kept my phone.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: You said your battery had failed.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: You removed the battery.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Modern phones do not have removable batteries. Listen to how her memory changes.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: It was my old blue phone. The back cover was tied with tape.

4.speaker: TARA
4.text: She had a blue phone like that.

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: Many people did.

4.speaker: TARA
4.text: Hers had white tape across the back. I put it there.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: A daughter repeating a detail does not prove force.

4.speaker: MOHAN
4.text: Why would Ma leave without us?

4.speaker: TARA
4.text: Mohan, don't call her that here.

4.speaker: MOHAN
4.text: You cannot stop me thinking it.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: Children should be taken inside.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: They are the children Raghav says she abandoned. Their presence is relevant.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: It is also cruel. Tara's school is close to the transport yard, isn't it? Public gossip can be difficult for a girl her age.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Do not bring my daughter's school into your mouth.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: I was expressing concern.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Powerful men often call a warning concern. Continue with your account.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Meera wanted work in Kota. She said her family watched every rupee. She said she wanted a life where nobody counted her steps.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: I wanted to buy Tara exam guides and Mohan new sandals. That is what I told you.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: You told me many things.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Then tell them what happened after the bus stand.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: You left with Shahid.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: You put me in his vehicle.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: I introduced two adults. I did not put anyone anywhere.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Was money discussed?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Transport costs money.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: That was not my question.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: No illegal payment was discussed in my presence.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: He counted notes inside the vehicle.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: She was outside the vehicle. Now she was inside. Another change.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: I was beside the open door. I saw bundles under the front seat.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Bundles can contain invoices. Transport businesses still use paper.

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: Meera, if this happened, why did you not return?

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Because I was not allowed to return.

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: For eighteen months? Not one message? Not one neighbour?

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Baba, I tried—

4.speaker: DEVRAJ
4.text: Do not use that word to make an answer disappear.

4.speaker: MOHAN
4.text: She came back. That is an answer.

4.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
4.text: The boy has more sense than this committee.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: Silence, or I will clear the courtyard.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Raghav, did you receive money for arranging Meera's travel?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: A small brokerage fee. Legal and ordinary.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: How much?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Two thousand rupees, perhaps. It was a long time ago.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: That is not the payment he is afraid of.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: There. An accusation without a number, a receipt or a witness.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Did Shahid pay you?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: No.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Did anyone connected to Shahid transfer money to you, your business or your relatives?

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: You may inspect every account for which you have legal authority.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: Ask him when it happened.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: When did what happen?

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: The payment. He knows the date.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: This is becoming theatrical.

4.speaker: COMMITTEE HEAD
4.text: Then end the theatre. Give the committee the date of your two-thousand-rupee brokerage.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: I cannot remember an ordinary fee after eighteen months.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: But you remember how long she sat, where she stood and what she said about her family.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: Because those details became important later.

4.speaker: MEERA
4.text: The larger payment was important immediately.

4.speaker: RAGHAV
4.text: There was no larger payment. The five lakh rupees were not even paid to me. They were paid on the third of May, twenty twenty-one.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Meera has not told police the amount. She only reported that money changed hands.

4.speaker: KAVITA
4.text: Yet you have just named the exact five-lakh payment date before Meera told police either the amount or the date.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: This door. Break this door, and I will show you where they kept me.
5.sfx_cue: metal latch rattling, fists striking wooden door

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Nobody breaks my property. Show me a warrant or leave my courtyard.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Open the room. Refuse again, and I will seal the entire floor until a magistrate decides who enters it.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: You police people arrive after eighteen months and speak as though dust committed the crime.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: I slept behind that door. I counted the cracks above the window every night.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: I have never rented a room to any Meera.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: Then we have travelled to Kota for another false memory.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: She knew the staircase without anyone showing her.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: That does not mean she lived here.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: There are seventeen steps. The sixth one is broken at the edge. The room has a green wall and no fan regulator.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Every room upstairs has a green wall.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: And the broken sixth step?

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: People notice stairs while climbing them.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: There is a water stain shaped like a hook beside the window.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Enough. The room was rented to another woman.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Name.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Sarla.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: That is what Shahid called me in front of strangers.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: I do not know any Shahid.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: You answered before I asked whether you knew him.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Because she has repeated the name three times in my courtyard.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: Madam, open the room. Either her details are correct, or we end this journey here.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: You are waiting for me to fail.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: I am waiting for evidence that does not change whenever a new person arrives.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: If she is wrong about one stain, will you take her away?

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: No. One room does not decide her identity.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Good. Then decide it somewhere else.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Constable, call the local station and request a property seal.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Wait. There is no need to spoil everyone's day over one empty room.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: It was not empty when you collected rent.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: I collected rent from Sarla's guardian.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Guardian? She was an adult tenant.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: That was the word he used.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Who was he?

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: A transport man. I do not remember every customer.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: You remember enough to change the word landlord into guardian.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: I remember rent paid on time. That is all.

5.speaker: NARRATOR
5.text: The lock opened. Meera stepped inside before anyone invited her.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: The cot was against this wall.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: It is against the other wall now.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Move it. Please. There should be writing behind the headboard.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: There is no writing. I repaint between tenants.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: You did not repaint behind the cot.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Constable, move it carefully.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: There are lines on the wall.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Thirty-four vertical marks. Some crossed in groups of seven.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: I marked the nights when he took the outside bolt off.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: Anyone could make marks.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: The last group stops halfway because Shahid came early.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: She is inventing meaning for scratches.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Then tell me why this bedroom door has an outside bolt.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: For luggage security.

5.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
5.text: Luggage does not sleep in the room and cry at night.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Who said that? Come upstairs and give your name.

5.speaker: SECOND VOICE FROM COURTYARD
5.text: We all heard someone. None of us wants our name in your ledger.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: They heard me.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: They heard a person. I will take individual statements before deciding more.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Look above the window. The hook-shaped stain.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: It is there.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: Stains survive tenants. It could be older than her claim.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: Why do you make every correct answer smaller?

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: Because you are a child, and somebody must protect you from wanting too much.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: I only want Ma.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: You want this woman to be Ma.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: She knows things Ma knew.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: Things can be told.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Tara is right to be afraid.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: Do not tell me what I feel.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Then I won't.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Meera, what else should be in this room? Something removable, not a wall or stain.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: A brass button under the window ledge. I pushed it into a crack.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Now we will search for buttons in an old building?

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Yes. Evidence is often smaller than the person hiding it.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: Why a brass button?

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: It came off Mohan's brown sweater. I found it in my blouse pocket after they brought me here.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: The sweater with the bear?

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: No. The one you hated. Brown wool, wooden train stitched near the collar.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: It scratched my neck.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: You cried whenever I pulled it over your ears.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: What did you sing?

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: Mohan, not here.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: What did you sing when I would not put my head through?

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Little train, little train, wait beside the door. Mohan has one stubborn head, but Ma has counted four.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: No. You missed the next part.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: I don't... I thought you had forgotten it.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: Sing it properly.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: One for anger, one for tears, one that asks for sweets. The fourth comes out when morning starts, and kisses both my cheeks.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: Ma.

5.speaker: TARA
5.text: Mohan—

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: She is my Ma. I am saying it where everybody can hear me. She is my Ma.

5.speaker: VOICE FROM COURTYARD
5.text: The boy has recognised his mother.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: A lullaby proves memory, not identity.

5.speaker: MOHAN
5.text: Then my memory is better than yours.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: I found the crack beneath the ledge.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: There is no button. But the plaster has been disturbed recently.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Repairs happen. You cannot arrest a wall.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: Where is the rental ledger?

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: You have seen the room. Leave my records alone.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: The room was rented under another name. The ledger is now part of the verification.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Old books are downstairs. Some pages may be damaged.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: If one page is missing, the entire ledger goes into evidence.

5.speaker: NARRATOR
5.text: Downstairs, the landlord opened a steel trunk and lifted out a red cloth book.
5.sfx_cue: steel trunk lid opening, paper rustling

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Here. Sarla. Room twelve. Rent paid in cash.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: The tenant column contains a different name, but this signature does not say Sarla.

5.speaker: MEERA
5.text: That is my name.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: No. No, that date cannot be right.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: Read it aloud.

5.speaker: LANDLORD
5.text: Twenty-first of June, twenty twenty-one.

5.speaker: DEVRAJ
5.text: By then, our family believed Meera had already been cremated.

5.speaker: KAVITA
5.text: And beside that date, the rental ledger contains Meera's signature.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Nobody touches the evidence table. The first person who crosses this rope leaves the verification.
6.sfx_cue: crowd pressing against rope, police whistle

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Then remove Mohan. He is already beside her chair.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: I will sit with my Ma.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: He may sit there. He may not touch the documents.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: I want my death certificate placed in front of me.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: It is an official record, not an object for public handling.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Place it inside the transparent cover, Babulal.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: If the cover tears, I will record who ordered this.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Record my designation correctly.

6.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: Yesterday she was locked outside her house. Today her death certificate gets a police chair.

6.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: Paper has always received more respect than women here.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: This is supposed to be evidence, not entertainment.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Correct. That is why you will not interrupt each item.

6.speaker: NARRATOR
6.text: One hour earlier, a sealed fingerprint envelope had fallen through the station slot into an empty records room. Nobody saw it arrive.

6.speaker: NARRATOR
6.text: Now Kavita placed that envelope beside the certificate recording Meera as dead.
6.sfx_cue: paper envelope placed on wooden table

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The open verification has five parts. Documents. Fingerprints. Family testimony. Physical identifiers. Contradictory records.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: And no final declaration until every objection is entered.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Agreed. Read the first document.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: School admission register. Student name, Meera. Father's name, Devraj. Original left-thumb impression attached.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: That register is old. Ink spreads.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Your objection is noted before the result has even been opened.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: He is frightened.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: I am frightened of another mistake being made in public.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: The first mistake was made in public too. You called a burned body your daughter, then called your living daughter a stranger.

6.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: She has spoken the truth plainly.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: You saw no face in that hospital either.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: I was not asked to identify the body.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Enough. Babulal, the second document.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: Ration-card amendment form. Signed by Meera. Right-thumb impression taken two years before her disappearance.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The forensic unit compared both archived impressions with the fresh prints taken at the station.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Was the unit told what result the police expected?

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The samples were coded. The examiner received no names.

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: What does the envelope say?

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: You may come closer, Tara. Do not cross the rope.

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: I can hear from here.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The fresh left-thumb impression matches the school register impression at fourteen corresponding ridge characteristics.

6.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: Fourteen points. Say what that means.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: It means the old and new left-thumb impressions were made by the same person.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: Ma's thumb remembers her, even if Nana does not.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: A child should not humiliate his grandfather before a crowd.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: You humiliated Ma before a bigger crowd.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Mohan, sit down.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: I am sitting.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Then sit quietly.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: All right, Ma.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The right-thumb impression also matches the ration-card form.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: Both archived documents existed before the disappearance. Their dates and storage entries are verified.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: What about the Kota ledger? It carries her signature after the cremation.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: That is the contradictory-record section. We will reach it.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Conveniently last.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Conveniently in the order I announced before you objected.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Physical identifiers. Meera, show both hands.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: The tattoo is on my left hand. It has always been on my left hand.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: The hospital photograph shows the burned body's tattoo beside the right wrist.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The photograph number and hospital intake number are legible. There is no reversal in the image.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: The black thread looked identical.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: A black wrist thread is not unique. A tattoo on the opposite hand is a material discrepancy.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: You did not touch the body, Baba. You would not even touch my hand at the station.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: The body was burned. I was told not to disturb it.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Who told you?

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: A hospital worker. I don't... there were several people speaking at once.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Name or description?

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: No.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Then your statement remains that an unidentified worker discouraged a physical check.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: I was grieving.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: And I was alive.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Family testimony. Tara, what did Meera know inside the house?

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: She knew where my first school ribbon was hidden.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Someone could have told her.

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: I did not tell anyone the tin was behind the loose brick.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Did she find it without directions?

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: Yes.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Do you recognise her as your mother?

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: I recognise things she knows. I am not ready to say more.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: She does not have to say more today.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Mohan?

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: She sang the sweater song. Only Ma knew the fourth head kisses both her cheeks.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Did she prompt you?

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: No. I tested her, and she finished it.

6.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: He called her Ma in Kota. We all heard about it.

6.speaker: MOHAN
6.text: I will call her Ma here too. Ma. Ma. Ma.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The repetition is unnecessary, but the answer is recorded.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Let him repeat it. They repeated that I was dead for eighteen months.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Now the Kota rental ledger.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: The tenant name is Sarla. The signature appears to say Meera. The date is the twenty-first of June, twenty twenty-one.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Meera provided six fresh signatures under observation this morning.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: A person can alter a signature.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Yes. That is why the examiner also compared letter formation, pressure and stroke order with older records.

6.speaker: TARA
6.text: And?

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The Kota signature appears copied. Its strokes stop and restart where Meera's natural signature remains continuous.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Someone signed my name.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: That is the present forensic opinion. The ledger does not disprove your identity.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Opinion is not certainty.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Neither was your identification of the body, yet it was accepted as certainty.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: Madam, the register cannot simply be rewritten during a village meeting.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: I am not ordering a rewrite. I am ordering the death certificate marked disputed pending formal correction and further inquiry.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: That requires recorded grounds.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Record them. Two fingerprint matches. Correct private family knowledge. A physical tattoo discrepancy. A copied rental signature. Consistent identification of the Kota room.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: You are declaring her genuine because the crowd wants a miracle.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: No. I am announcing that the evidence strongly supports Meera being alive and genuine.

6.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
6.text: Say it again. Let the people at the back hear.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The woman standing here is strongly supported by documentary, fingerprint and family evidence as Meera.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Babulal, bring me the paper that buried my name.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: It remains government property.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Then let the government correct itself where everyone can see.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: I have a red disputed-record seal. Once stamped, the certificate cannot be used as an uncontested proof of death.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Apply it.

6.speaker: DEVRAJ
6.text: Wait. If you stamp that, the original murder case—

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: Will be reviewed on evidence. Not protected from embarrassment.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: The seal is inked.

6.speaker: MEERA
6.text: Do it.

6.speaker: KAVITA
6.text: The police officially acknowledge that the original identification of the burned body may have been wrong.

6.speaker: BABULAL
6.text: Meera's death certificate is now sealed and formally marked disputed.

7.speaker: COURT GUARD
7.text: Back. All four of you, back against the wall.
7.sfx_cue: court corridor, handcuffs and crowd murmurs

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Let me speak to the judge. Two minutes. That woman is alive.

7.speaker: COURT GUARD
7.text: You will speak when your case number is called.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: Our case number belongs to a dead woman. Bring her inside.

7.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
7.text: Eighteen months in jail, and now the murdered woman walks into court.

7.speaker: COURT GUARD
7.text: Quiet. This is a court corridor, not the village square.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: They were jailed in my name. I want to hear why.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Meera... you are really standing here.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: Yes. Now tell me how my life became your murder charge.

7.speaker: irfan
7.text: Salim, stop. You don't know who is listening.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Everyone listened when they called us murderers.

7.speaker: pintu
7.text: And everyone watched when police dragged us from our houses.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: You will each get an opportunity. Do not coordinate your accounts here.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: Coordinate? We have shared one cell and one accusation for eighteen months.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Then eighteen months should have taught you to answer separately.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: My answer was separate. I gave it on the first night.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: What answer?

7.speaker: salim
7.text: That Raghav sent us to the accident site.

7.speaker: irfan
7.text: Salim!

7.speaker: COURT GUARD
7.text: No shouting between prisoners.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: Say it again. Clearly.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Raghav told us where to go, before the police arrived there.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Do not add another word in this corridor.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Madam, I already said every word. Police wrote it down.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: Case number forty-seven. State versus Salim, Naresh, Pintu and Irfan.

7.speaker: COURT GUARD
7.text: Move.

7.speaker: NARRATOR
7.text: Four men entered together. For the first time, the woman they were accused of murdering entered behind them.
7.sfx_cue: chains and footsteps enter high-ceilinged courtroom

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Who authorised this crowd? Clear the centre aisle.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: The villagers are witnesses to the identity dispute, Your Honour.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: They are spectators until summoned. Spectators remain silent.

7.speaker: WOMAN IN GALLERY
7.text: They called Salim a butcher in front of his mother.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: One more interruption, and the gallery will be emptied.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: The police request permission to place a new development on record.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Proceed.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Meera's death certificate was formally marked disputed yesterday.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: Then open these cuffs.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: You will not instruct the court.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: No, sir. I... I only mean, there cannot be her murder if she is here.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: A disputed certificate is not an acquittal. It is a reason to examine the record.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: Examine the part where they used my name without asking whether I was alive.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: You will be heard after the case history is read.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: The prosecution alleged that the four accused killed Meera and burned her body near the east quarry road.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: They were detained after being located near the accident site.

7.speaker: pintu
7.text: Because somebody called us there.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Who called you?

7.speaker: pintu
7.text: Salim said there was a crashed vehicle. He said people might need help.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Salim, where did you get that information?

7.speaker: irfan
7.text: Sir, may I speak privately before he answers?

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: No. The question was not addressed to you.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Raghav came to the repair shed that morning.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: He said a vehicle had gone off the east quarry road.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: He told us to reach it before the traffic police took everything away.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: What time?

7.speaker: salim
7.text: A little after six. The tea stall had just opened.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Was Raghav with you at the site?

7.speaker: salim
7.text: No. He gave the location, then left in his white pickup.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: Why did all four of you go?

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Pintu knew the road. Naresh had a tow chain. Irfan came because I asked.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: We found a burned vehicle, one body, and no living passenger.

7.speaker: pintu
7.text: Police arrived within twelve minutes. Too quickly for that road.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: How were the accused connected to the alleged victim?

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: The original case diary says they were found beside the body and gave inconsistent accounts.

7.speaker: naresh
7.text: We were questioned separately after being awake all night.

7.speaker: irfan
7.text: They kept asking which one of us lit the fire.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: I kept saying Raghav sent us.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Did you sign that statement?

7.speaker: salim
7.text: Every page. My thumbprint is below the last line.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Sub-inspector, locate the first-night statement.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Court clerk, give me volume one.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: Arrest memos, seizure list, site sketch and medical forms.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Where are the individual statements?

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: After page eighty-six, according to the index.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Page eighty-six is followed by page ninety-three.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: Check the supplementary volume.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: Supplementary volume begins with laboratory correspondence.

7.speaker: meera
7.text: Ask who removed seven pages.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: The court will ask the questions.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: My statement was five pages. The others signed one page each.

7.speaker: pintu
7.text: Seven pages.

7.speaker: irfan
7.text: Don't... don't say anything else, Salim.

7.speaker: salim
7.text: You stayed quiet for your brother. I stayed quiet because I trusted the file.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: Clerk, read the index entry aloud.

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: Accused statements, pages eighty-seven through ninety-three, recorded on the night of arrest.

7.speaker: JUDGE
7.text: And those pages are not in either volume?

7.speaker: COURT CLERK
7.text: No, Your Honour.

7.speaker: kavita
7.text: The original case diary contains the index, but Salim's statement is missing.

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: These men will not be returned to silence inside the old murder file.

8.speaker: COURT CLERK
8.text: Your Honour, the prison transfer order is ready.

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: Read it aloud. Their families have waited long enough to hear it.

8.speaker: COURT CLERK
8.text: All four accused are to be produced in the reopened identity inquiry.

8.speaker: naresh
8.text: Does that mean we leave jail today?

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: It means the old accusation may no longer bury new evidence.

8.speaker: salim
8.text: And my missing statement?

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: The police will reconstruct its custody and record your account again.

8.speaker: irfan
8.text: In open court?

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: Under protection, if the investigating officer finds a credible risk.

8.speaker: irfan
8.text: I need protection for my brother, not for myself.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Give me his details before you return to custody.

8.speaker: pintu
8.text: We came to court as four murderers.

8.speaker: naresh
8.text: We are still in cuffs.

8.speaker: pintu
8.text: Yes. But now the court has to ask who sent us there.

8.speaker: WOMAN IN GALLERY
8.text: Naresh, your daughter can hear you!
8.sfx_cue: gallery erupts in cries and applause

8.speaker: JUDGE
8.text: Order. The four accused will be brought into the reopened inquiry, not hidden inside the old case.

8.speaker: NARRATOR
8.text: Before noon, an old missing-person complaint reached the court records tray. No named witness saw who placed it there.
8.sfx_cue: single paper slides into metal tray

8.speaker: COURT GUARD
8.text: Clear the doorway. The next matter cannot enter through your shoulders.
8.sfx_cue: court veranda crowd and approaching bus horn

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Please, move. I came from the neighbouring district for the burned woman.
8.sfx_cue: hurried footsteps, cloth bag buckle rattles

8.speaker: COURT GUARD
8.text: Which burned woman?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: The woman cremated as Meera. She may be my sister.

8.speaker: meera
8.text: What is your sister's name?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Kesar.

8.speaker: meera
8.text: Come inside. Do not tell this story in a doorway.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: You are Meera?

8.speaker: meera
8.text: Yes.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Then whose ashes did they give your family?

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: Nobody has established that those ashes belonged to her sister.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Are you the man who identified the body?

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: I am her father.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: That was not my question.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Janki, come to the side room. Bring every document you have.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: I brought her missing-person complaint and three photographs.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: When did Kesar disappear?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: In June, twenty twenty-one. She left for a hospital appointment and never returned.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: What made you connect her to this body?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: A court notice said the woman wore a black thread around her wrist.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: Many women wear black thread.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Kesar's had three knots and a small copper bead.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: The original hospital note mentions a black thread. It does not mention a bead.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Then look at the photograph before they cut it away.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: The photograph is disturbing. Confirm that you still want to view it.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: I have imagined worse every night for seventeen months. Show me.

8.speaker: meera
8.text: You don't have to prove your love by looking at a burned face.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: No. I have to prove the police searched under the wrong woman's name.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Only the wrist photograph first.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: The thread is twisted twice here. Kesar always did that after bathing.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: That cannot identify a person.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Neither could you, apparently.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: You arrived ten minutes ago. Do not judge what that day was.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: My sister vanished. Your daughter returned. I know exactly what these days are.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Enough. We test records, not grief against grief.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Did Kesar have a tattoo?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: No permanent tattoo. A childhood burn mark below her left thumb.

8.speaker: meera
8.text: The body photograph showed a tattoo on the hand opposite mine.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: The skin was damaged. The mark was difficult to read.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Was her face visible?

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: This interview is being conducted by the police.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: You answer very carefully for a grieving father.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Janki, what hospital appointment was Kesar attending?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: A wrist dressing. The burn had reopened after field work.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Which hospital?

8.speaker: janki
8.text: The district civil hospital. I wrote it in the complaint.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Babulal, bring the unidentified-body intake sheet from the original file.

8.speaker: babulal
8.text: The original is brittle. I will place it in a clear sleeve.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Why is there a red line across the name box?

8.speaker: babulal
8.text: The patient arrived unidentified. Meera's name was added after Devraj's identification.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: After police asked me to identify my daughter.

8.speaker: meera
8.text: You identified a thread and a damaged mark. Not me.

8.speaker: devraj
8.text: I identified what I could.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: The intake sheet records one female patient, severe burns, no usable facial identification.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: Read the number at the top.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: No... read it once more.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: That number was written by the hospital clerk on Kesar's appointment slip.

8.speaker: babulal
8.text: Your missing-person complaint is in the records tray. It has the same number in the reference box.

8.speaker: kavita
8.text: Show her the complaint.

8.speaker: janki
8.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight. This hospital intake number is the number on Kesar's missing-person complaint.

9.speaker: MAN IN CROWD
9.text: Devraj, look at your daughter before you deny her again.
9.sfx_cue: village courtyard crowd and microphone feedback

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I will not answer a mob.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Then answer me. Touch my hand and say who I am.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: This public spectacle proves nothing.

9.speaker: mohan
9.text: It proved enough when you called Ma a stranger in front of everyone.

9.speaker: tara
9.text: Mohan, stand beside me.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Nobody will touch or surround Devraj. He is here to correct his identification statement.

9.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
9.text: He sent four men to jail with that statement.

9.speaker: MAN IN CROWD
9.text: And he would not even touch Meera at the station.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Silence. Public humiliation will not repair public error.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: No. But public truth may begin to repair it.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: You asked me to attend a formal verification. Conduct it formally.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: I intend to. Stand at the microphone.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I can speak from here.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Your original identification was accepted publicly. Your correction will be heard publicly.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: You have already marked the certificate disputed.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: A red seal corrected a document. It did not correct your words.

9.speaker: NARRATOR
9.text: Devraj crossed the same courtyard where his refusal had made Meera a stranger.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: The microphone is unnecessary.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: The people at the back disagree.

9.speaker: janki
9.text: So does the family of the woman you identified.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: The body has not been proved to be Kesar.

9.speaker: janki
9.text: No. But the hospital number proved my complaint was ignored.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Today's question is narrower. What did Devraj actually see?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I saw the body police brought from the accident site.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Could you identify the face?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: The face was... it was severely burned.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: That was not the question.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: No. I could not identify the face.

9.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
9.text: He never saw her face, yet he called it Meera!

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: One more interruption, and I will end the verification.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Do not end it. I waited eighteen months for this answer.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Devraj, what feature did you rely upon first?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: A dark mark on the hand.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: You described it as Meera's tattoo.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: That is what I believed it was.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Meera's tattoo is on the opposite hand.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I know that now.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: You knew which hand when I was a child. You paid for the medicine after it became infected.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: The body was covered. The room smelled of smoke and chemicals.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: What other feature did you rely upon?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: The black thread around the wrist.

9.speaker: janki
9.text: Kesar wore one with three knots and a copper bead.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I did not see a bead.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Did Meera always wear a black thread?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: She wore one during illness and after temple visits.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Not every day. I had removed mine before I disappeared.

9.speaker: tara
9.text: It was tied to the bedpost. I found it after she was gone.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: You never told me that.

9.speaker: tara
9.text: You never asked me. You told me Ma was dead.

9.speaker: mohan
9.text: Then you burned someone and said she was Ma.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Mohan, you are too young to understand that day.

9.speaker: mohan
9.text: I understood the day you would not touch her.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Devraj, did any doctor certify a facial identification before you signed?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: No.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Did police have fingerprints or DNA linking the body to Meera?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Not then.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Did you see clothing you personally recognised?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Only burned cloth. Nothing certain.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Then state why you signed the identification.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Police said the accident matched the time she vanished.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: They said the four men near the site had changed their stories.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: They showed me the hand, the thread, and her name already written on a form.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: My name was already written?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: In pencil, at the top. I thought they knew more than they told me.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: That detail is not in your original statement.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Nobody asked who wrote the name first.

9.speaker: janki
9.text: They gave you a name, and you gave them certainty.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: They asked whether it could be my daughter.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: And you turned could be into yes.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I was afraid.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Of what?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Of taking an unclaimed body home. Of refusing, then learning I had abandoned you twice.

9.speaker: tara
9.text: So you accepted the first answer that ended the waiting.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Yes.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: State it without explanation. Did you identify the face?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: No.

9.speaker: kavita
9.text: Was your identification based on certainty?

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: No. It was based on fear and grief.

9.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
9.text: Then Meera was shamed because her father was frightened.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Yes. She was shamed because I was frightened.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: At the station, I asked you to touch my hand.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I remember.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: You called me an impostor where my children could hear later.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: I was trying to protect the decision I had already made.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Not me. The decision.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Yes.

9.speaker: mohan
9.text: Touch her hand now.

9.speaker: tara
9.text: No. Let Ma choose whether he may.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: You may touch my hand after you answer one question.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Ask it.

9.speaker: meera
9.text: Who am I? Say it so the whole village hears you.

9.speaker: devraj
9.text: Meera is my daughter. I was wrong to call her a stranger.

10.speaker: NARRATOR
10.text: By the next morning, Devraj's apology had reached every courtyard. So had another fact. Kavita had found the five lakh rupees.
10.sfx_cue: police station gate clanging shut, crowded voices

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: You froze my cousin's cooperative account without one question to me.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: I am asking now. Explain the deposit dated the third of May, twenty twenty-one.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: It was for a tractor.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: You said the money was not paid to you. You did not say it was sitting with your cousin.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Because it was not my account. That distinction is usually understood by adults.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: Speak without insulting my daughter.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Your family arrangements change very quickly, Devraj.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: My mistake does not make your answer true.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Good. Everyone has finished performing. Sit down, Raghav.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I prefer to stand.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Then stand beside the account statement, where everybody can see both of you.

10.speaker: NARRATOR
10.text: The public desk became a hearing without a judge. Villagers filled the doorway. Meera stood where she could see Raghav's face.
10.sfx_cue: ceiling fan rattling, low crowd murmur

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Cooperative account ending four one nine two. Account holder, Raghav's cousin. Deposit, five lakh rupees. Date, third of May, twenty twenty-one.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Correct. A commercial deposit is not a crime.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Who deposited it?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: A tractor buyer.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Name.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: The papers are old. I cannot remember every farmer who asks for machinery.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: But you remembered the date in front of the village. Eighteen months later. Before I told police the amount.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I remembered because the accusation was repeated to me.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: By whom?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: People talk.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Name one person.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: This is becoming theatrical.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: No. Theatre gives the audience a lie and tells them it is a lie. You asked us to call yours truth.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I arranged a tractor inquiry. That is why the date stayed in my mind. There. Your mystery is finished.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: You arranged it?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I connected the buyer to my cousin. I did not receive the money.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: So when you said you knew nothing about the payment, that was false.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: No. You are flattening a commercial transaction into a confession.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: You knew the date because you arranged the deposit.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I knew a tractor booking date. Meera later attached her story to it.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: My story? You watched Shahid count the notes twice. Bundles of five hundred. You took one bundle back because it was short.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: That is an allegation from a woman whose rental signature has already been called false.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Copied. The examiner called it copied, not false. Do not improve the evidence while quoting it.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Then arrest the handwriting.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: The account statement includes a deposit slip reference. Your cousin signed the slip. The depositor field contains initials.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Initials are not a person.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: They match the initials used by Shahid on two transport receipts.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Many people share initials.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Then bring Shahid here.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: You seem very eager to see the man you claim imprisoned you.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: I am eager for him to see that I came back.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: And that she did not come back alone.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Please. A father's courage, after signing his daughter dead, is not evidence.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Quiet. Raghav, threats disguised as insults remain threats when twenty people hear them.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I threatened nobody. I am concerned Devraj may damage his health by becoming emotional.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: My health is not in your account.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: The tractor. Manufacturer?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: A standard farm model.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Manufacturer?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I don't... I did not handle delivery.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Model number?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Ask my cousin.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: We did. He said you chose the vehicle and brought the buyer.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Then he is mistaken.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Your cousin remembers you. You remember the date. Neither of you remembers the buyer.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Or the tractor.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: A booking can be cancelled.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Then there should be a refund.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Perhaps there was.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: There was not.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Then the amount may have been adjusted against another vehicle.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Which vehicle?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: You have the account. You tell me.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: I have every debit for the next six months. No tractor dealer received money from this account.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Cash settlement.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Five lakh rupees in cash, with no receipt?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Village commerce does not always ask police permission.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Neither did you, when you took me to Kota.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: You went willingly.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Then why did you remove my phone battery?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I did not.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Why did you tell Tara I had chosen another life?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I did not speak to Tara.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: You spoke to me. You said searching would shame the children.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: I offered practical advice to a distressed family.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: You offered us silence. My father accepted it. I will not.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Raghav, was the deposit connected to Meera?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: No.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Was it connected to Shahid?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: No.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Was there a tractor?

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Yes.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Then give me its chassis number by five this evening.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: That deadline is unreasonable.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: You have remembered the transaction for eighteen months. Five hours is generous.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: And if an old office cannot find one number?

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Then I ask the district transport office whether your tractor ever existed.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: You are treating clerical delay as criminal intent.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: I am treating five lakh rupees as five lakh rupees.

10.speaker: NARRATOR
10.text: At five, Raghav returned with no chassis number, no invoice and no buyer. Kavita returned with a certified search.
10.sfx_cue: rubber stamp striking paper, evening crowd murmuring

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: A registration search proves nothing. Farm vehicles remain unregistered for months.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Not this dealer's vehicles. The dealer says no order was placed by you, your cousin or this account holder.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Dealers lose records.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: Banks do not lose the date stamped on a deposit.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: Say the dates together.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: The money entered your cousin's account on the third of May, twenty twenty-one.

10.speaker: meera
10.text: And I disappeared?

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: On the fifth of May, twenty twenty-one.

10.speaker: raghav
10.text: Coincidence is not evidence.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: No. The account is evidence. The dates are evidence. Your changing answers are evidence.

10.speaker: devraj
10.text: And the tractor?

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: The account received the five lakh rupees two days before Meera disappeared.

10.speaker: kavita
10.text: But the tractor was never registered.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Do not let her follow us. If she is really my mother, she will know where to go.
11.sfx_cue: garden hoe biting dry earth, children whispering

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: She is Ma. You heard the lullaby.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You wanted her to be Ma before she opened her mouth.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: And you wanted her to be a stranger.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I wanted nobody to leave twice.
11.sfx_cue: small clay object scraping against metal

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: There. The bird still has one wing.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Put it back. Deep. Then cover the soil properly.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: What if she does not remember?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Then I stop making excuses for her.

11.speaker: NARRATOR
11.text: Tara buried the clay bird again before breakfast. By noon, she had gathered half the village beneath the neem tree.
11.sfx_cue: village courtyard crowd, neem leaves rustling

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Why are all these people here?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Because everybody watched when Grandfather called you a stranger. They can watch this too.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: Tara, if this is another public test—

11.speaker: tara
11.text: It is my test. You had yours. Police had theirs. Now I decide.

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: What are the rules?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Nobody answers for her. Nobody gives hints. Nobody tells me that fingerprints are enough.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: Fingerprints are enough.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Mohan.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: Fine. I will not give hints.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Ask.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Not yet. First, tell everyone what you want from this house.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You and Mohan.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: That is not an answer. We are not objects kept in a cupboard.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I want to live where my children do. I want to cook badly in my own kitchen. I want to know which schoolbook Mohan has lost this week.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: Geography.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: No hints.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: And I want Tara to stop standing near every doorway, ready to run if I say the wrong thing.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I do not do that.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You are doing it now.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Maybe I like the doorway.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You hated doorways. You said they made every room look unfinished.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: That could be in a diary.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You never kept a diary. You wrote one page, then tore it because Mohan drew a buffalo over your secret.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: It looked better.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: This is not the test.

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: Then begin it.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Before you disappeared, I made something. I hid it. Nobody from police found it. It is not in any statement.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: What did you make?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I said nobody answers for her.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: I was only— yes. Ask her.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: What was it?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You made many things. A clay cup that leaked. A horse with five legs.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: So you do not know.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I did not finish.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Then finish.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: A bird.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: She knows.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: What colour?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: None. You refused paint because you said real sparrows did not wear festival colours.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: How many wings?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Two when you made it. One after you dropped it beside the stove.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Where did I hide it?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You told me you threw it away.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Then you do not know where it is.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I know you were lying.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: That is not a place.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You had soil beneath your fingernails. Red soil, not the grey dust near the wall.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: There is red soil in three parts of the courtyard.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You came inside with neem leaves caught in your braid.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: There are neem leaves everywhere.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Not in the kitchen. Not behind the water drum. Under this tree.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Where under the tree?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Near the root shaped like a bent knee.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: There are four roots.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: The eastern root. Three handspans from the trunk.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Why there?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Because that was where I buried your first tooth after you asked whether a new one could grow from the ground.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Nobody knew about the tooth.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You and I knew.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I never told Mohan.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: You told me this morning.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: About the bird. Not the tooth.

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: Has the location ever appeared in a police statement, school record or family testimony?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: No.

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: Did anyone tell Meera before this test?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: No. I buried it again myself.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Again?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I checked that it was still there.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You dug it up without me.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You were dead.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I know what the register said.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: No. You don't... you do not know what that did here. Every person brought food. Every person spoke softly. Then they went home.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: And you stayed.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I stayed with a brother who woke up calling for you. I stayed with Grandfather, who said questions were disrespectful.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: Tara, I was ashamed and afraid.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: I am not asking you.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You stayed. I was not here. Both are true.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: If I accept you, what happens when police call tomorrow? What happens when Kota calls? What happens when Raghav walks free?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I answer the police. I go to Kota if the inquiry needs me. And every time, I tell you before I leave.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: People promise that when they want entry.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Then do not give me trust today. Give me one night.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: One night?

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Let me sleep in my house. If you wake, I will be there. If Mohan calls, I will answer. Tomorrow, you decide again.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: She can sleep beside us.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: The house is hers too.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You do not decide that.

11.speaker: devraj
11.text: No. I don't. I have decided enough for all of you.

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: There is no police restriction preventing Meera from staying with her children. The identity certificate remains disputed, not cancelled.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: So the choice is mine?

11.speaker: kavita
11.text: The personal choice is yours. The evidence has already made its own.

11.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
11.text: The girl has tested her enough. Let the mother enter.

11.speaker: SECOND VOICE IN CROWD
11.text: We all watched her refuse the woman. We should hear her answer now.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Nobody speaks for me.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: They did that to you after I disappeared, didn't they?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Every day.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Then take your time.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Dig where you said.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You want me to dig it up?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Three handspans. Eastern root.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: I will help.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: No. She knows the place.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: The earth is loose here.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Because I buried it again this morning.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I feel something.
11.sfx_cue: clay clicking against a metal bangle

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: Take it out, Ma.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Your bird. One wing. And the beak is still too large.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You said it looked like a crow.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: You did not speak to me for two hours.

11.speaker: tara
