11.text: Three hours.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Then I owe you one hour.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You owe me more than that.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I know.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Tonight, you sleep in the room with us. Not near the door. Mohan kicks when he dreams.

11.speaker: mohan
11.text: Only sometimes.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: And if police call, you wake me before you go.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I will.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Say it properly.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: I will not leave this house without telling you.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Everyone heard that?

11.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
11.text: Everyone heard.

11.speaker: tara
11.text: Good.

11.speaker: meera
11.text: Tara... may I touch you?

11.speaker: tara
11.text: You do not need to ask me that, Mother.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Remove Kota from my statement. Today. Before the court receives another copy.
12.sfx_cue: records office door banging open, ledger pages fluttering

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: You cannot withdraw a place as if it is a spelling mistake.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I can correct a statement taken under public pressure.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: You signed every page.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Then give me a fresh page.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: This is a records office, not a washing stone.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Your shop is on estate land, isn't it? Paperwork can become tiring when boundaries are reviewed.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: My shop has nothing to do with this file.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Of course not. I was expressing concern for your workload.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Express it from the other side of the counter.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Sub-inspector. Excellent. Tell your clerk that citizens may amend inaccurate statements.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: He is not my clerk. And an amendment does not erase the first statement.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Then attach my correction. Meera was never in Kota with me.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: You stood before the committee and said I travelled there willingly.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I repeated what I had heard. The crowd was shouting. Questions overlapped.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Nobody asked whether you had been to Kota. You volunteered details about a transport fee and the payment date.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I was confused by the accusation.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: You were clear enough to call me a woman who abandoned her children.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I withdraw that too.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: You cannot return eighteen months with one sentence.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I am correcting an error. You should be pleased.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: I will be pleased when you say where you left me.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I left you nowhere, because I did not take you anywhere.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Your correction will be recorded as a changed account. State the complete version.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I met Meera near Dharmapur. I did not transport her to Kota. I did not introduce her to Shahid.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: How do you know Shahid's name?

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: It has been shouted through the village for days.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: Not in front of you.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Villages have ears even when police pretend they do not.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Continue.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I know nothing about a room in Kota. I know nothing about confinement. The five lakh rupees were a tractor deposit unrelated to Meera.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: You did not bring the tractor record.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: The transport search was incomplete.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: It covered every district registration for twelve months after the deposit.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Then perhaps the buyer changed his mind.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: Yesterday, the tractor existed. Today, the buyer changed his mind. Tomorrow, will the account disappear?

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Your confidence is impressive for somebody asking the state to restore her name.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: The state marked me dead. I learned not to borrow confidence from paper.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Paper also marked the certificate disputed.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: After you interfered with it.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: After police ordered a correction.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: You are very brave behind that counter.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: I am... I am careful behind it. That is different.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: And today he will remain careful while you sign your changed statement.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Gladly.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Read the last line aloud.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I state that Meera was never in Kota with me, and any earlier statement suggesting otherwise was made under confusion.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Date and time.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: The twenty-fourth of November, twenty twenty-two. Ten forty in the morning.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Sign.
12.sfx_cue: pen scratching, rubber stamp striking paper

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Finished.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: No. Now I attach it to your first statement.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Do that. The latest statement controls.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: The court decides what controls.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Then I have nothing further to say.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Wait.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: For what?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: You said you were never in Kota with Meera.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: That is what you just stamped.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Your vehicle number. Does it remain D H seven, C, eight two six four?

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Why?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Yes or no.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: That vehicle was sold.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: After the dates under inquiry. Was that its number in May twenty twenty-one?

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Yes. Hundreds of people knew it.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: I saw the number this morning.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: In which file?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Not a police file. An old travel register sent from Kota after a transport office audit.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Travel registers contain copying errors.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: You have not seen this one.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: I know how roadside clerks write.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Bring the register.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: It is in the lower records room.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Before you produce some mouldy book, remember that a vehicle number does not identify its driver.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: You recognised the number before he opened the book.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: He spoke my old vehicle number aloud.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: And you became frightened.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Do not mistake irritation for fear.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Stay here.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Am I detained?

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: No. You may leave. Your statement and vehicle number will remain.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: A courteous threat is still a threat.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Then you recognised the courtesy.

12.speaker: NARRATOR
12.text: Babulal returned carrying a register so large he held it against his chest with both arms.
12.sfx_cue: heavy footsteps, thick ledger thudding onto counter

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Kota commercial travel register. Entry gate, east depot. The binding was never closed after the final page.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Why was it sent to Dharmapur?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Vehicle numbers were being compared with local permits. The packet arrived seven months ago. Nobody indexed it.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: So it sat unattended for seven months. Excellent chain of custody.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: It is an administrative register, not seized evidence. We will verify it with the Kota office.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: The page carries their seal and the attendant's initials.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Find the vehicle.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: There are two entries. Arrival on the fifth of May, twenty twenty-one, at nine twenty in the evening.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: The day I disappeared.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: She knows the date. Anyone could have written the number later.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: The ink crosses the page ruling. It was written before the next entry. What name is beside it?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: No driver's name. Only vehicle number, arrival time and passenger count.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Passenger count?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Three.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: A commercial vehicle carries passengers. Astonishing.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: Raghav drove. I sat in the back. Another man sat beside him.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: That is Meera's assertion. The register independently records three occupants.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: It records a number somebody copied from a passing vehicle.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: The entry is open.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Meaning?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Arrival was recorded, but there is no departure on the same line. That is why I noticed it.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Then it proves the vehicle never left.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: No. The departure was entered four pages later, after the attendant changed shifts.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Read it.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Vehicle D H seven, C, eight two six four. Departure, two fourteen in the morning. Passenger count, two.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: It arrived with three and left with two.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Passenger counts are guesses.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Why is the departure line marked in red?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: The vehicle was linked to an unclosed inquiry. A woman reported missing from the same depot corridor.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Which woman?

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: You said this register was a copying error. Why do you need her name?

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: Because you are building another performance around a red line.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: There is a complaint reference in the margin.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Whom did the complaint concern?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: A second woman connected in the complaint to an alleged buyer. She was last seen near the east depot.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: The same place Raghav said he never took me.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: This proves no person was inside my vehicle.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: No. It proves your vehicle entered and departed Kota while you now deny being there.

12.speaker: raghav
12.text: On different dates, perhaps.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: The date is written on both pages.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: Read the departure date.

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: The sixth of May, twenty twenty-one.

12.speaker: meera
12.text: And the missing woman?

12.speaker: babulal
12.text: Her complaint gives the same night.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: The register shows Raghav's vehicle left Kota that night.

12.speaker: kavita
12.text: The same night the second alleged buyer disappeared.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: Stop. Nobody touches this envelope until all four seals are read aloud.
13.sfx_cue: sealed envelope slapped onto wooden table

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Read Kesar’s result first. I have waited long enough for everyone else’s name.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: And read mine in front of my children. They buried my name in public.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Both results will be read. Nobody leaves midway.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: Seal one, district forensic laboratory. Seal two, collection officer. Seal three, magistrate’s court. Seal four, receiving clerk.
13.sfx_cue: wax seals tapped one by one

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: The samples were not mixed? I need that stated clearly.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: They were collected separately, coded separately and tested twice.

13.speaker: tara
13.text: Then open it.

13.speaker: mohan
13.text: Ma, hold my hand.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: I am holding it.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: Reference sample A belongs to Devraj. Reference sample B belongs to the woman identifying herself as Meera.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: She is Meera. You may read the report exactly, but she is my daughter.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Let the paper say it too.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: The probability of biological parentage between sample A and sample B exceeds ninety-nine point nine nine percent.

13.speaker: mohan
13.text: What does that mean? Say it normally.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: It means the laboratory confirms that Meera is Devraj’s biological daughter.

13.speaker: tara
13.text: Say her full status too. She is alive.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Meera is alive, and this report scientifically confirms her identity.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: I called my own daughter an impostor. This paper does not remove that shame.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: No. It does not.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: But it removes the excuse of anyone who still calls you a stranger.

13.speaker: VOICE IN CORRIDOR
13.text: The dead woman’s sample is next.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Do not call her that. Call her Kesar, if the report gives me that right.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: The second comparison uses preserved tissue from the burned body and Janki’s reference sample.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Her black thread had three knots. There was a copper bead between the second and third.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Those details supported the inquiry. DNA will decide the identification.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: I know. I am only... I am trying to remember her before you read it.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Remember her.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: The preserved tissue is not genetically related to Devraj.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: Then the woman I signed for was never my daughter.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: Correct.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: And me? Please, do not stop there.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: The sibling analysis supports a full biological sister relationship between Janki and the deceased woman.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: How strongly? Give me the number.

13.speaker: LAB TECHNICIAN
13.text: The likelihood ratio exceeds twenty-eight thousand to one.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: So she was Kesar.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Yes. The woman cremated under Meera’s name was Kesar.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: They searched for Meera’s killers while my sister lay inside Meera’s death certificate.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: And while I was alive inside another woman’s name.

13.speaker: tara
13.text: Mother, does this finish it? Can nobody take you away now?

13.speaker: meera
13.text: It finishes who I am. It does not finish what was done.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Correct. Identity is settled. Criminal responsibility is not.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: I want Kesar’s name returned today.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The civil registrar has been directed to prepare the corrected certificate.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Directed is not delivered.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Then we will collect it ourselves.

13.speaker: NARRATOR
13.text: One hour later, the laboratory report reached the district records counter before anyone could soften its language.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: I need the original death entry, the disputed seal order and both certified DNA pages.
13.sfx_cue: rubber stamps knocking in a drawer

13.speaker: janki
13.text: You already have them.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: I have copies. Today, copies are not enough.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: They were enough when the office declared me dead.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Yes. That was wrong.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Say the exact wrong.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: The burned body was registered under Meera’s name without scientific identification.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: And I signed the identification.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: You did.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: After Meera’s name was already written on the form.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Which officer entered that name, Babulal? Promise nothing. Read the movement sheet.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: The receiving duty officer wrote it. The entry says, identity supplied by telephone before family arrival.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Whose telephone call?

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: The caller field contains one name.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Read it.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Raghav.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: He gave them Meera’s name before I saw the body?

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Twenty-three minutes before you signed.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Then my father did not begin the lie.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: I still completed it.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The duty officer physically wrote Meera’s name. The record says Raghav supplied it by telephone.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: He named my sister as Meera before anyone had identified her.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: That is what the contemporaneous entry records.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: There is another attachment. The east depot complaint mentioned in the Kota register inquiry.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: The second woman.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Read only what the document establishes.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: The complaint identifies the missing woman as Kesar. A depot camera note records Raghav’s former vehicle number.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Kesar was the second woman linked to that alleged buyer?

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Yes. The complaint gives her name, the vehicle number and the east depot location.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: His vehicle arrived with three occupants and left with two.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The depot timing places Kesar outside that vehicle before it departed Kota.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: He left her there.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The records show his vehicle departed after Kesar was dropped near the east depot. They do not yet prove what happened after that.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: But they prove why the third occupant was missing when the vehicle left.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Yes. Kesar was the third occupant. Raghav’s vehicle left with two after leaving her behind.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: And later she was found at the accident site under Meera’s name.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The DNA report establishes that the burned body at that site was Kesar.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: I can now cancel the incorrect body-name entry and create Kesar’s lawful death record.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Do it where I can see your hand.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Cause and criminal responsibility remain subject to investigation. Identity is confirmed by DNA.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Write her name without Meera’s name beside it.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Kesar. Female. Identity confirmed.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Again.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: Kesar.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: She waited inside my grave. I waited outside my house.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Neither of you chose that.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: The corrected certificate is ready.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: Give it to me.

13.speaker: babulal
13.text: This certifies the death under Kesar’s own name. The previous certificate naming Meera remains suspended for cancellation by the court.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: For the first time since she vanished, an office has written my sister’s name correctly.

13.speaker: tara
13.text: And Mother’s name?

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Tomorrow, the court will hear the DNA report, the money trail and the false identification entry together.

13.speaker: mohan
13.text: Will the four men come too?

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: Yes. The court has ordered all four produced.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Then let everyone who saw four murderers see four living men.

13.speaker: devraj
13.text: And everyone who saw a stranger will see my daughter.

13.speaker: janki
13.text: What does the final laboratory conclusion say? Not the certificate. The last paragraph.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: It says the remains match Janki’s biological family and do not match Devraj’s family.

13.speaker: meera
13.text: Read the consequence.

13.speaker: kavita
13.text: The DNA report places Kesar at the accident site and Meera nowhere near the death scene.

14.speaker: COURT OFFICER
14.text: Remove their handcuffs. The murder charge has just lost its dead woman.
14.sfx_cue: courtroom handcuff chain dropping onto rail

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: Do not say that unless the judge has signed it.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: We want the order. All four names. Read every name.

14.speaker: COURT OFFICER
14.text: Stand quietly. The court is sitting.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: This is the reopened matter concerning Meera’s identity, Kesar’s remains and the prosecution of four accused men.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: I request permission to stand with my children.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Granted.

14.speaker: mohan
14.text: Ma, they really took the chains off.

14.speaker: tara
14.text: Not all of them. Their ankles are still locked.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Court officer, remove every restraint unless you have a separate lawful warrant.

14.speaker: COURT OFFICER
14.text: There is no separate warrant.

14.speaker: pintu
14.text: Then use the key.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: Wait... wait until the order. We have been promised doors before.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: He is right. Read it first.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The DNA report confirms that Meera is alive and identifies the burned remains as Kesar.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The factual basis for alleging that these four men murdered Meera no longer exists.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: Then we leave today?

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: You will hear the full order without interruption.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: Yes, Your Honour.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The prosecution relied upon a body identification now disproved by DNA, a missing statement and inconsistent case records.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: No lawful purpose is served by preserving a murder case for a person who stands alive before this court.

14.speaker: VOICE IN GALLERY
14.text: They spent all that time in jail for nothing.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Say it louder. The village called us murderers louder than that.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Silence in court.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The murder proceedings against Salim, Naresh, Pintu and Irfan are quashed.

14.speaker: pintu
14.text: Quashed means finished? Not bail?

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: Finished. The murder case cannot keep you in custody.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: All four of us?

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: All four.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: No reporting every week? No police permission to leave Dharmapur?

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Not under this quashed case.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: And my missing five-page statement?

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Its disappearance will remain part of the departmental and criminal inquiry.

14.speaker: pintu
14.text: We entered this building as four murderers.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Then let the officer say how we leave.

14.speaker: COURT OFFICER
14.text: You leave as free men. There is no subsisting custody order against any of you.

14.speaker: VOICE IN GALLERY
14.text: Salim and the others are innocent of Meera’s murder.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: There was no murder of Meera.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: I am sorry my stolen name became your prison.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: You came back alive. You did not put us there.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: Will my brother receive protection now? I gave the court what I knew.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: The protection direction remains active. Your release does not cancel it.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: Good. Then open the gate.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Before release processing, the court will address the remaining evidence concerning Raghav.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: I came voluntarily. I have answered every proper question.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: You changed your Kota statement after the travel register was requested.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: I corrected an error. Correction is not concealment.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: Your former vehicle entered Kota with three occupants and left with two.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: A vehicle number does not identify passengers.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: The east depot record identifies Kesar as the third occupant left near the depot.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: That is an interpretation.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: The DNA report identifies Kesar as the woman later found burned at the accident site.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: DNA cannot place me at an accident I did not witness.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The court has not said it can.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Then there is no ground to detain me.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: There is also the five-lakh-rupee deposit made two days before Meera disappeared.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: A tractor payment.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: No tractor was registered. No purchase invoice exists. No delivery occurred.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Registration can be delayed.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: For eighteen months?

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: The buyer may have abandoned the transaction.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: Then why was the money never returned?

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Ask the account holder.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: We did. Your cousin states that you controlled the passbook and withdrawal slips.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: He is protecting himself.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: The first withdrawal occurred forty minutes after your vehicle entered Kota.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Coincidence is still legal.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: You knew the five-lakh date before I said the amount.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: You have repeated that performance enough.

14.speaker: tara
14.text: Do not call my mother a performance.

14.speaker: VOICE IN GALLERY
14.text: He called her an impostor too.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: No. I called her that. I was wrong, and I said so before this village.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: Raghav supplied her name for the burned body before I reached the hospital.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: You signed the form, Devraj. Be careful where you move your shame.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: I am not moving it. I am naming the man who placed the lie in front of me.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The movement sheet records that a duty officer wrote Meera’s name after receiving it by telephone from Raghav.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: That entry proves only that someone used my name.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: The call originated from the number registered to your transport office.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Many people used that office.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: You may contest the evidence during investigation and trial. Today, the court considers preservation of evidence and risk of interference.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: I have remained in Dharmapur throughout.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: You filed a changed statement, denied Kota and described the travel register as fabricated.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: The register predates this inquiry. Its paper, ink and binding were verified.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: A clerk defending a neglected register is not an expert.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: No. The forensic document examiner is.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: The application for custodial arrest is allowed concerning the money trail, false identification information and connected disappearance inquiry.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: On suspicion?

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: On recorded financial evidence, contradictory statements and a documented risk of interference.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Meera’s allegation remains an allegation.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: And it will be investigated as one. Turn around.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: You are arresting the man who brought her to safety.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: You brought me to Kota. You did not bring me home.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: This village will tire of your story.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: Your hands, please. The court has been courteous enough to provide an order.

14.speaker: VOICE IN GALLERY
14.text: Raghav is leaving in chains while the four men walk free.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Look at me, Raghav.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: I do not take instructions from you.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: You sent us to that road. Your name stayed outside the file. Ours went inside a murder charge.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Then enjoy your release carefully. Dharmapur has a long memory.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: So does a recorded threat made inside a courtroom.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: It was advice.

14.speaker: JUDGE
14.text: Remove him.

14.speaker: raghav
14.text: Meera, this does not prove your entire story.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: No. It proves enough to stop you walking away today.

14.speaker: NARRATOR
14.text: By noon, the hearing moved from the courtroom to the public records desk, where the first wrong had been written.
14.sfx_cue: large register dropped onto public counter

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: The court order directs immediate cancellation of Meera’s death entry.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Not another disputed stamp. Cancellation.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Cancellation. The red line will cross the full entry, and the order number will be written beside it.

14.speaker: tara
14.text: Let us see every word.

14.speaker: mohan
14.text: Can I stand on the chair? I cannot see.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Come here. I will lift you.

14.speaker: janki
14.text: And Kesar’s certificate?

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Entered under her own name, with the DNA confirmation attached.

14.speaker: janki
14.text: Show the seal.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Here.

14.speaker: janki
14.text: Kesar. Not unidentified. Not Meera.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Kesar.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: The same villagers watched me refuse my daughter’s hand.

14.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
14.text: We watched.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: Then watch this too.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: Meera is my daughter. I identified the wrong body, and I was wrong to call her a stranger.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Father.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: I will not ask you to erase what I did.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Good. Stand beside me while they erase what the register did.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Our release orders are stamped.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: Four orders. I counted twice.

14.speaker: pintu
14.text: The outside gate is open.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: My brother is waiting beyond it.

14.speaker: kavita
14.text: Walk through together. The crowd must see all four of you leave without restraints.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Meera, come with us to the gate.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: First, I need to watch my death end.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Red line through the old entry.
14.sfx_cue: pen dragging slowly across register page

14.speaker: mohan
14.text: It is gone?

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Legally cancelled.

14.speaker: tara
14.text: Write the new entry clearly.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: The court has supplied the final wording.

14.speaker: janki
14.text: Read it before you write.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: One living person restored. One deceased person correctly identified. Four accused released from a case without a murdered Meera.

14.speaker: salim
14.text: Write it.

14.speaker: VOICE IN CROWD
14.text: Make room. Let all four men reach the gate.

14.speaker: naresh
14.text: No chains.

14.speaker: pintu
14.text: No guards holding our arms.

14.speaker: irfan
14.text: No murder case behind us.

14.speaker: mohan
14.text: Ma, they are free.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Yes.

14.speaker: tara
14.text: And you are not dead.

14.speaker: meera
14.text: Not in this house. Not in this village. Not on that page.

14.speaker: janki
14.text: My sister has her name.

14.speaker: devraj
14.text: My daughter has hers.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: Final entry complete. I will read it exactly once.

14.speaker: babulal
14.text: The official register now records one final fact: Meera is alive, Kesar was the woman cremated, and all four accused are free.
